claims.text: Regulatory limits on credit card fees under the CARD Act reduced overall borrowing costs by an annualized 1.6% of average daily balances.
Regulatory limits on credit card fees reduced borrowing costs by more than 5.3% for consumers with FICO scores below 660.
Regulatory limits on credit card fees caused no offsetting increase in interest charges.
Regulatory limits on credit card fees caused no reduction in the volume of credit.
The CARD Act saved consumers an estimated $11.9 billion per year.
Disclosing interest savings from paying off balances in 36 months produced a small increase in the share of accounts making the 36-month payment amount.
Disclosing interest savings from paying off balances in 36 months produced no evidence of a change in overall payments.

evidence.description: Difference-in-differences estimates show regulatory limits on credit card fees reduced overall borrowing costs by an annualized 1.6% of average daily balances.
Subgroup analysis indicates a borrowing cost decline of more than 5.3% for consumers with FICO scores below 660.
Analysis finds no evidence of an offsetting increase in interest charges following the CARD Act implementation.
Analysis finds no evidence of a reduction in the volume of credit following the CARD Act implementation.
Aggregated estimates calculate that the CARD Act saved consumers $11.9 billion a year.
Evaluation of the 36-month payoff disclosure nudge detected a small increase in the share of accounts making the 36-month payment value.
Analysis detected no evidence of a change in overall payments resulting from the 36-month payoff disclosure nudge.

methodologies.name: Difference-in-differences research design
methodologies.description: Compares changes in outcomes over time for regulated consumer credit cards to unregulated small business credit cards using account-level panel data.
datasets: Panel data set covering 160 million credit card accounts
conditions: Consumer credit cards subject to 2009 CARD Act regulations
Small business credit cards not covered by the 2009 CARD Act
